comment: Decisions resolved at the gate, not a quality rejection - the review passed. All twelve registry entries are RESOLVED at v6, the clarification report is at v6, and three conventions were amended: SC-5 (10kb body limit), SC-9 (audit event carries event/userId/requestId only, best-effort after commit), AD-6 (taxonomy extended with UnsupportedMediaTypeError and PayloadTooLargeError, mapping gains 413, US-001 named as the Story that creates errors.ts with four subclasses). Re-run SPECIFICATION to consume them.

FR-18 confirmed: the four JWT variables are removed from .env.example. Nothing this Story ships reads them, and SC-3 keeps them out of src/config/env.ts until the Story that validates each - US-002 re-adds them together with the code that reads them. This was flagged at the gate twice and is now decided rather than read as tacit consent. The four Minor findings of review v11 are accepted as design inputs for API_DESIGN and IMPLEMENTATION_PLANNING, not as blockers: m-1 (no component row owns the translation of express.json() errors into PayloadTooLargeError and ValidationError, while the 415's owner is named) is the one with real downstream weight.

comment: Rejected on PLAN_REVIEW:p-3. Step 3 states an outcome the mechanism it names cannot produce: it asks for fileParallelism false scoped to tests/integration while unit tests stay parallel, but fileParallelism is a top-level test option and the current flat vitest config covers both trees in one include, so as written it would either serialize the whole suite or scope nothing. Revise IMPLEMENTATION_PLANNING to name a supported Vitest project/configuration mechanism (test.projects is the one PLAN_REVIEW confirmed by probe at vitest 4.1.11) that disables file parallelism for tests/integration only and preserves unit-test parallelism, and resubmit for HUMAN_PLAN_APPROVAL. p-3 is reassigned from IMPLEMENTATION to IMPLEMENTATION_PLANNING by this decision and stays RAISED until the revised plan names the mechanism. Not decided here and still owed at the next gate: PLAN_REVIEW:p-1 (D-4 commits .env.test citing neither PC-10 nor PC-1), DESIGN_REVIEW:e-1 (spec v14 stale against AD-6), PLAN_REVIEW:p-4 (SC-3 line 178 cites AC-5 for the error body) and the plan's two Open Questions. The other three review findings, p-2 and p-5 and the review's four required plan edits, may be folded into the same revision.

comment:
Rejected at HUMAN_PLAN_APPROVAL. The plan is sound; one decision goes the
other way.

DECISION ON PLAN_REVIEW:p-1 (Open Question 3). The !.env.test negation is
DECLINED. The recorded fallback is taken: CI supplies DATABASE_URL as a
workflow variable and .env.test stays local-only. AGENTS.md Prohibited, PC-10
final bullet and PC-1 second bullet are left uncrossed. Accepted cost: PC-1's
named deliverable stays uncommitted and the connection string lives in two
places.

SCOPE OF THE LOOP-BACK. Step boundaries do not move and no module file list
changes. But D-4's own claim that "either outcome leaves the file list
unchanged" (plan line 263) is inaccurate: under the fallback .gitignore is not
modified at all, since .gitignore:28 (.env.*) already ignores the file, so that
row leaves Files To Modify rather than changing. Rows to revise: 437 (.env.test
"committed"), 470 (.gitignore, drops), 420 (impact-reconciliation row 2), 987
(R-3's closure parenthetical), 1023 and 1024 (Configuration Changes), plus D-4's
body, Open Question 3, Step 3, and the CI file's description. The
process.env.DATABASE_URL -> .env.test resolution order in D-10 is unchanged;
only which side is committed changes. Nothing else in v3 is reopened: p-6 and
p-7 stay verified, p-8 stays owed to IMPLEMENTATION.

comment:
Decision at TEST_WRITING, BLOCKED on TEST_WRITING:B-2. The workflow advances
to IMPLEMENTATION.

TEST_WRITING has delivered what this stage can deliver. All 71 tests are
authored, execute, and fail for the correct reason; every Acceptance Criterion
AC-001..AC-007 has mapped coverage; format:check and check:cycles pass. The
residual 4 typecheck and 30 lint errors are 100% attributable to one file,
src/lib/prisma.ts, which cannot be stubbed because PrismaClient is a generated
type.

B-2 is ACCEPTED rather than resolved, and it is accepted with a specific
expectation, not waived: IMPLEMENTATION Step 2 writes prisma/schema.prisma and
runs prisma generate, which makes PrismaClient exist and clears all 34
diagnostics as a side effect of ordinary planned work. No separate remediation
is owed. IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION must confirm that typecheck and lint
actually reach 0 once Step 2 lands; if they do not, B-2 reopens.

The three alternatives were declined for now, not rejected on their merits.
Reordering the plan so the schema precedes TEST_WRITING (option b) is the
structural fix and remains the right answer for future Stories whose tests
touch persistence - it is declined here only because it costs a loop-back to
IMPLEMENTATION_PLANNING and a plan re-review to buy something IMPLEMENTATION
Step 2 delivers in the next stage anyway. Extending the stub authorization to
cover a schema (option c) was judged disproportionate: a schema carries a
migration and is a design artifact, not a signature. The ESLint carve-out
(option d) was declined because it was verified insufficient - it silences
lint but not typecheck, so the suite still would not compile.

Known consequence, stated so it is not rediscovered: the Definition of Done
sequence and the Stop hook stay red until IMPLEMENTATION Step 2 lands. That is
an accurate report of where the work is, and it must not be made green by
editing eslint.config.js, adding eslint-disable comments, typing prisma as
any, or skipping the four affected test files. RECONCILIATION should read this
event rather than treating the red interval as drift.

comment: Roll back to TEST_WRITING, on instruction from the user in session. IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION returned BLOCKED naming TEST_WRITING as the responsible stage for IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION:V-1 - a defect in the authored test tests/integration/auth-register-audit.test.ts, not in production code. stage-map.yaml gives IMPLEMENTATION_VERIFICATION no automated edge to TEST_WRITING (its only loop_back is changes_required -> IMPLEMENTATION), so this human-directed route is recorded the way a gate rejection routes to on_reject: skill null, decided_by human. test-writer re-enters at attempt 4 to fix V-1 only: scope the EC-4 failure to the audit path (inject a rejecting auditLog dependency, or make the logger.info stub throw only for the user.registered payload and delegate other calls, or restore the stub before the response settles), keep both existing assertions, change no production file and weaken no assertion. Everything else in the verification is green: build/typecheck/lint/openapi/cycles all 0, migration applies clean, 73/73 tests pass, all 7 ACs behaviourally VERIFIED. On the next green suite, IMPACT_ANALYSIS:R-4, DESIGN_REVIEW:e-2/d-4 and IMPLEMENTATION_PLANNING:R-P1 become dischargeable - the integration evidence they waited on now runs.
